title: Throughput drop after fused-attention rollout during autoscale event — follow-up & action items
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a scheduled canary rollout of the fused-attention optimization (PR #2345) into runtime-1.24 we observed a sudden throughput drop (~30-50% p50 token/sec) for a small subset of customers between 2025-02-10 23:40 and 2025-02-11 01:10 UTC. The drop coincided with an autoscaler event that added new GPU instances to a Dedicated pool to handle increased traffic.

Timeline (high level):
- 23:30 UTC: Autoscaler triggered scale-up for instance pool (burst traffic).
- 23:35 UTC: Canary rollout of fused-attn enabled for model family raven-* (10% of servlets).
- 23:40 UTC: Monitoring alerted: token throughput down, request latency up for affected nodes.
- 23:48 UTC: Ops rolled back fused-attn flag for canary cohort; throughput recovered gradually by 00:10 UTC.
- 00:25 UTC: Postmortem triage started; rollbacks confirmed the feature interaction.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by profiling):
1) Fused-attention kernel had a micro-architectural performance cliff for sequence lengths > 2048 when running on CUDA compute capability 7.5 drivers with our quantized kernels. This was not visible in unit perf tests which used compute capability 8.6 images.
2) The autoscaler added older-instance types (compute capability 7.5) due to placement constraints. Those instances were assigned fused-attn kernels by new kernel-selection heuristics introduced in PR #2310.
3) Continuous batching + scheduler changes increased average effective batch sequence length (more prefix aggregation), pushing many requests into the pathological case.
4) The fused kernel execution path fell back to a slower copy+split implementation on 7.5 with extra memory traffic, increasing per-token latency and reducing throughput.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rollback: Reverted fused-attn feature flag for canary and scheduled rollback for remaining cohorts.
- Autoscaler temp policy: Pin autoscaler to prefer compute capability >= 8.0 nodes for raven-* models until mitigation complete.
- Rate control: Applied conservative max-batch-size 32 ingress limit for affected model family.

Evidence & artifacts:
- Profiling traces: flame graphs showing copy overhead (link below).
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 (fused-attn), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2310 (kernel selection heuristics).
- Dashboards: throughput per-token, kernel-type distribution by instance type, and per-instance sequence-length histogram (links below).

Repro steps for engineers:
1) Spin up instance type with compute capability 7.5 (internal image: rwinf/gpu-cc75:prod).
2) Deploy raven-small quantized model with fused-attn enabled and send synthetic traffic with seq lengths 1024-4096 and continuous prefixing enabled.
3) Observe increased memory copies and latency; collect nvprof traces and kernel logs.

Why existing tests missed this:
- CI perf matrix covered model x seq-length but used CC 8.6 builders; cross-driver coverage missing.
- Canary gating validated correctness and basic p99 latency but did not exercise sustained continuous-batching profile with live autoscaler-induced instance heterogeneity.

Next steps and long-term fixes are listed in action_items.
action_items: Owner: Daniel Kim — 2025-03-05 — Revert kernel-selection heuristic change in PR #2310 and add guard clauses to avoid selecting fused-attn on known-affected compute capabilities until validated.

Owner: Priya Rao — 2025-03-12 — Add CI perf matrix job covering combinations: [model family raven-*, seq lengths {512,1024,2048,4096}, compute capabilities {7.5,8.0,8.6}] and fail build on >10% regression vs baseline.
Owner: Platform SRE (Jorge Mendes) — 2025-02-25 — Add autoscaler placement constraint flag and an override to prefer cc>=8.0 for high-priority model pools; publish operational config in runbook.
Owner: Research/Applied ML (Leah Wong) — 2025-03-10 — Characterize fused-attn microbenchmarks across quantization settings, and produce a compatibility matrix for release notes.

Owner: Runtime Observability (Aisha Patel) — 2025-02-28 — Instrument kernel-selection telemetry persisted to traces and dashboards (kernel variant, cc, batch-size, seq-length). Create alert when p50 token/sec drops >20% and kernel distribution shifts >15% within 15m.

Owner: DevEx (Samir Patel) — 2025-03-15 — Update canary rollout playbook to include a perf gating step with synthetic continuous-batching workload and autoscaler simulation before enabling fused kernels globally.
Owner: QA (Nina Park) — 2025-03-08 — Create regression test harness that repros the exact incident traffic profile and runs nightly against staging with mixed instance pool types.
